theme: North Shore smoked lake fish becomes a brining-and-smoking creature with a coal-heart belly and kiln-rib fins.

evolution_design.regional_evidence: Duluth-based Northern Waters Smokehaus describes its own smoked Lake Superior lake-trout practice and local smokehouse history. This is a first-person food-culture source, not an endorsement or claim that the dish originated there.
evolution_design.original_invention: A fish-shaped cooking spirit grows its own broad smoker ribs and coal belly; no fish is shown burning or carrying a cooker. The dark typing expresses the creature hiding its coal-heart behind closed ribs.

body_growth.body: A compact fish-bodied ember with a broad curled tail, two thick cheek fins and one large pale salt-crust brow; a single dark belly opening contains its coal eye.
body_growth.silhouette: Compact sideways ember-fish, crescent tail and large salt brow.

body_growth.body: The body becomes taller and deeper, supported by two thick fin-feet. Three broad hinged rib-plates curve over the belly like a smoke chamber, while a wide slotted tail acts as its bellows and the true face emerges above the chamber.
body_growth.silhouette: Upright deep-bodied fish spirit with solid rib chamber and a large fan-bellows tail; feet distinguish it from a swimming recolor.

silhouette_concept: Compact sideways ember-fish, crescent tail and large salt brow. → Upright deep-bodied fish spirit with solid rib chamber and a large fan-bellows tail; feet distinguish it from a swimming recolor.
habitat: Duluth harbor food stalls and inhabited shore-side cookfire areas.

proposed_routes.placement: Southern rest district beside a future food NPC, outside the wild forest core.
proposed_routes.status: encounter proposal only; no map or story mutation

sources.title: Northern Waters Smokehaus, About
sources.supports: First-person Duluth smokehouse history and Lake Superior smoked lake trout.

nonduplication: Unlike ore-freighter boilerF060 or generic fire-fish: the family grows salt brow, hinged smoking ribs, fin-feet and bellows tail. No steel hull, funnel or conventional fish with flames pasted on.
